title: Pentagon confirms Fort Hood terrorist's firing squad execution will be livestreamed: 'Details will follow'
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Pentagon confirms Fort Hood terrorist's firing squad execution will be livestreamed: 'Details will follow'

The Pentagon confirms Fort Hood terrorist Nidal Hasan's firing squad execution will be livestreamed, according to a Pentagon official.

"Special Report" anchor Bret Baier reports that Pentagon officials have announced that convicted Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan's execution by firing squad will be livestreamed Dec. 3.

The Pentagon confirmed to Fox News Digital on Thursday that the firing squad execution of convicted Fort Hood terrorist Nidal Malik Hasan will be livestreamed, allowing the public to witness the military's first execution in more than six decades.

"It will be livestreamed. Details will follow," a War Department official told Fox News Digital.

The execution is scheduled for Dec. 3 at Fort Hood, Texas.

FORT HOOD SURVIVOR SHOT IN HEAD VOWS TO WATCH TERRORIST FACE HISTORIC FIRING SQUAD

The Pentagon confirmed to Fox News Digital that the firing squad execution scheduled for Dec. 3 would be livestreamed. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

Hasan, a former Army major, killed 13 people and wounded 32 others when he opened fire on unarmed soldiers and civilians after shouting "Allahu Akbar" at Fort Hood on Nov. 5, 2009. He was convicted in 2013 and sentenced to death for the massacre.

President Donald Trump approved the use of an Army firing squad, following War Secretary Pete Hegseth's recommendation. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell previously announced the decision on X, declaring, "Judgment day for Hasan has finally come."

If carried out, Hasan's execution would be the first by the U.S. military since 1961 and the first military execution by firing squad since 1945. Hasan remains on military death row at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas.
